conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Lee, one of your oncology team members. You're here for your 20th cycle of high-dose methotrexate. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’m doing okay. I’ve been feeling pretty stable since my last treatment. No headaches or weakness.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great to hear. We’ll be giving the methotrexate tonight, starting around 11 PM. Before that, we’ll start IV fluids to help protect your kidneys and keep your urine alkaline.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Last time I had some nausea with Zofran. Is that still the plan?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Actually, we’re switching to fosaprepitant this time. It tends to work better and causes fewer headaches than Zofran. We hope it helps you feel even better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that sounds good. I really didn’t like those headaches.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll monitor your urine pH closely to make sure it stays above 8.5. That helps the methotrexate clear safely from your body.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And when does the leucovorin start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: About 24 hours after the methotrexate finishes. It helps protect your healthy cells from the chemo. We’ll give it through your port.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. My foot pain has been acting up a bit. Can I still take my gabapentin?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, absolutely. Gabapentin is safe to continue. You can also use oxycodone as needed for breakthrough pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. And my asthma inhalers—I’ve been using them as usual.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, keep using your albuterol and the combination inhaler as prescribed. Your breathing sounds clear today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve also been on citalopram for my mood. It’s been helping.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s important to maintain. We’ll keep it on your list. Any feelings of low mood or anxiety lately?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Not really. I’ve been feeling pretty steady.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Glad to hear it. We’ll check your labs regularly to monitor your blood counts and kidney function.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re about to start the methotrexate infusion now. It’ll run for about two hours. Let us know if you feel any discomfort.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’m ready. No issues so far.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. The infusion went smoothly. Your urine pH has stayed above 8.5, which is perfect.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. I haven’t felt nauseous at all—maybe the fosaprepitant is working.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s excellent. We’ll draw your first methotrexate level later today to track how it’s clearing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had an MRI this morning, right? Was everything okay?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, the MRI showed no signs of lymphoma recurrence. The changes in your brain are stable, which is exactly what we want to see.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, that’s such a relief. Thank you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also saw some chronic sinus inflammation, but nothing new or concerning. It’s unrelated to your lymphoma.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had sinus issues for years. Nothing to worry about, I hope.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, it’s not related to your treatment. We’ll leave it to your primary doctor unless it flares up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your methotrexate level came back at 0.17 micromolar. That’s declining well, so we’re on track.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that a safe level?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s low enough that we can safely continue with leucovorin and IV fluids for a bit longer and plan for discharge tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Will I need to take leucovorin at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, because your level is clearing so well, you won’t need oral leucovorin or bicarbonate after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s one less thing to manage. What about aspirin? I was off it last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We held it during your stay for safety, but you’ll restart it at home. We used heparin for clot prevention while you were here.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Right, because of my history with blood clots.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We always take extra precautions with that. Your leg has no swelling, which is good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—you’re cleared to go home today. You tolerated everything very well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful. No more IVs?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, we’ll remove the IV before you leave. Just continue your regular meds, including aspirin, citalopram, gabapentin, and your inhalers.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And I’ll keep using oxycodone if my foot pain flares up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, as needed. And call us if you have any fever, unusual fatigue, or signs of infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will do. Thank you for explaining everything so clearly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re very welcome. You’re doing well with your treatment. We’ll see you for your next cycle in a few weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll be ready. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. Have a safe trip home.
